topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, setting expectations and context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Foundations and central role of C3 in complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core foundational concepts, naming conventions, and central C3 activation mechanism governing the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three activation pathways that converge to trigger the complement cascade on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the effector mechanisms through which activated complement destroys pathogens and mediates inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical manifestations and pathologies resulting from deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens evade complement destruction and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in biomedical applications.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing framing, concluding the lecture and previewing the next session on adaptive immunity.
